title: The 1949 jazz meeting and the High Society question
summary: At a National Jazz meeting on Carondelet Street Laurent and others were asked who originated the High Society variation, and he took George Baquet and others to the meeting.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Do you remember the High Society chorus? Who was the first one you ever heard play that little runs? You remember that?

Well, I'm going to give you the full definition of that. That was asked to me in a National Jazz meeting at 831 Caronelet Street in the year of 1949. I believe it was 40, 80 held that meeting at 831 Caronelet Street. People were all over. That same group came out to my place that very second or third night after they held that meeting. They came out to the happy land and while I was playing, sat down and had a nice time that night. They brought that same question up. They brought that same question up. See, who was the originator and composer of High Society? Well, George Bakke was there with me. Old Man Humphrey was there with me. I just had a new set of uniforms made. We had nice gray uniform, caps, shirt, ties, all the ties to match and everything.
Was George Bakke playing with you?
No, George Bakke came back home. It was his first trip back home from the time he had left home.

But I was very well acquainted with George Bakke. Sure. He was bumming all the while. He came back together first, me, George Bakke. I knew all of his people. And we went to the meeting. I taken him over in my car to the meeting. I taken Old Man Humphrey, Piku, no, yeah, Piku, George Bakke, myself, and Ernest Trapani. He was a great drummer also.
I didn't get to know him, but he... He died lately. He worked at that same bar room that George's sister had on. Yeah, that's it.
